newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Chile's Escondida union delays strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Escondida union delays strike vote.

text.p: Striking workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine postponed by two hours a vote Wednesday on whether to continue on the request of workers' wives who want the strike to go on, a union official said.

"The vote was postponed to 1200 local (1600 GMT) because there is a group of workers' wives who want to talk with the workers to change their minds and make them continue the strike," Pablo Godoy, of the Chilean Mining Confederation, which is advising the Escondida union, told Reuters.
Union leaders Tuesday recommended the workers accept the pay offer and and return to work.
Voting should be finished by 1700 local and the result known almost immediately, Godoy told Reuters by telephone from Antofagasta in Chile.
Godoy said he was advising workers to continue the strike.
The mine's 350-odd unionized workers stopped work Friday to demand progress in wage negotiations. The rest of the mine's 2,000-strong workforce did not join the strike.
Mine CEO Ken Pickering said Monday that the strike had slown down operations slightly but that output of both concentrates and cathodes was normal.
The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp Plc.
